vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: clipboard-memory
Version: 1.3.4

The clipboard-memory skill bundle provides a comprehensive interface for an AI agent to search and retrieve macOS clipboard history using the local 'clipmem' CLI tool. While accessing clipboard data is inherently sensitive, the bundle's behavior is transparent, extensively documented, and strictly aligned with its stated purpose of helping users recover previously copied information. The included diagnostic script (scripts/check-setup.sh) uses safe practices, such as sanitizing JSON input via Python before shell evaluation, and the SKILL.md instructions provide clear, non-malicious guidance for agent behavior without any evidence of exfiltration or harmful prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill's requirements and instructions are consistent with its stated purpose (local clipboard recall on macOS); it reads and manipulates a local clipmem archive and does not request unrelated credentials or network access.

dimensions.detail: Name/description ask to recall clipboard history on macOS and the skill requires only the `clipmem` binary and local access to the clipmem SQLite archive — this is proportionate and expected.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions instruct the agent to run `clipmem` read and management commands (recall, search, get, export, timeline, service status, settings, forget, purge, etc.). These are within scope but include local mutations (forget, purge, settings reset, app launch-at-login, app quit) and exporting raw bytes to disk; the agent should only perform mutations when the user explicitly asks and be cautious about `export --out`/`--force` which write/overwrite files.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Install uses a Homebrew formula (tap: tristanmanchester/tap), which is a third-party tap (moderate trust level). SKILL.md metadata also references a cargo install path (crates.io) though the registry install spec included here lists only brew — minor inconsistency to verify. No remote arbitrary archive downloads are present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or credentials. It only needs filesystem access to the local clipmem DB and the ability to run the `clipmem` binary, which matches its purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and default invocation settings. The skill does not request permanent/always-on inclusion or other skills' credentials. It may start/stop a local watcher service via `clipmem setup`/`brew services` when asked — appropriate for its domain.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is coherent: it uses the local `clipmem` tool to read and manage your macOS clipboard archive. Before installing, confirm you trust the `clipmem` project and the Homebrew tap (tristanmanchester/tap) or prefer the cargo release. Be aware the skill can: (1) read the clipboard database at ~/Library/Application Support/clipmem/clipmem.sqlite3, (2) export binary blobs (images, PDFs) to disk (watch for the output path and `--force`), and (3) perform local mutations (forget, purge, settings reset, stop/start the watcher) — only run destructive commands when the user requests them. If you want extra caution, inspect the installed `clipmem` binary source or install it from a provenance you trust, and review any `export` paths before allowing the agent to write files.
